resources.string: If a site breaks, write its domain here, one per line: it and every name under it are never blocked.
Names on a public ad and tracker list get no answer, in every app. The list is fetched through Shroudly and refreshed weekly.
Every app on this device goes through Shroudly.
Only the apps checked go through Shroudly
Every app goes through Shroudly, except the ones checked
Chosen: {count}; every other app goes straight out
Every other app, system apps too, goes straight out, past Shroudly. With none checked, every app goes through Shroudly.
An automation app asked to turn protection on, but Android lets other apps start it only when Shroudly\'s battery use is unrestricted. Tap to turn it on now.
An automation app asked to turn protection on, but the VPN has not been allowed yet. Tap to allow it and turn protection on.
Battery settings can stop Shroudly in the background and cut your connection. Let it run without battery restrictions.
Apps and Shroudly use IPv4 only, and apps learn at once that there is no IPv6 instead of waiting for it. For networks whose IPv6 is broken or slow.
Your phone turned Shroudly off. Tap to turn protection back on.
No internet: Shroudly cannot get through on this network right now, and Android is set to block connections without a VPN. Shroudly keeps trying.
The new mode is used the next time protection starts.

Shroudly runs as a proxy on 127.0.0.1:{port} (SOCKS5 and HTTP) and leaves the VPN to another app. Only apps set to use it go through Shroudly: the Wi-Fi network\'s proxy (host 127.0.0.1, port {port}) or an app\'s own proxy setting.
Every app goes through Shroudly. Android allows one VPN at a time, so another VPN app is disconnected.
Protection stopped because Shroudly could not reach the internet on this network, so your apps are connecting directly. Open Shroudly to try again.
Protection stopped because of an error, so your apps are connecting directly. Open Shroudly to start it again.
Proxy only is off. If this network\'s proxy is set to {addr}, set it back to None in Wi-Fi settings, or apps that use it cannot connect.
Proxy only: apps set to use 127.0.0.1:{port} go through Shroudly
Apps use TCP instead of QUIC (UDP port 443), which Shroudly gets through better. For networks that block QUIC or slow it down.
Tasker, MacroDroid and similar apps can turn protection on and off with a broadcast to the package {package}, action {action}.START, .STOP or .TOGGLE. While this is off, no other app can.
Protection comes on by itself after the phone restarts, once the VPN has been allowed.
A Shroudly tile in the panel at the top of the screen turns protection on and off with one tap.
The Shroudly tile is in Quick Settings.
Pull the panel at the top of the screen all the way down, tap the pencil (edit), and drag the Shroudly tile up among the others.
Shroudly needs the VPN permission to carry your apps\' connections.
Protection was switched off by Android, usually because another VPN app was turned on.
This network\'s proxy is set to {addr}, but nothing is running there, so apps that use it (Chrome among them) cannot connect. In Wi-Fi settings, open this network and set Proxy to None.
This network stops {app}\'s connections, and none of Shroudly\'s techniques got through. Use {app}\'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
{app} cannot reach its servers: this network blocks their addresses, and Shroudly cannot get around that without a server elsewhere. Use {app}\'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
That is not an IP address or a server name; type it like {example}.
The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
That is not a proxy address; type it like socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 or http://127.0.0.1:8080.
That address does not fit this kind; type it like {example}.
Every lookup Shroudly makes goes to this server. If it stops answering, Shroudly\'s encrypted DNS answers until it is back.
No answer ({error}). Not in use; check the address, or use it anyway.
Answered in {ms} ms (example.com: {address}). In use now.
Only the connections to this DNS server go through it: for a server that is blocked by its address. A SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, like socks5://127.0.0.1:1080.
Nothing else is asked, even when it does not answer: lookups then fail until it does. For testing a server, or when no other may see your lookups.
Their traffic goes straight out, past Shroudly: for example a game that does not need it.
Shroudly is free and open source under the MIT license: anyone can read, audit and build its code.
Count me in the live total

Sends a random number that changes every launch, so the app can show how many copies are running. It is only sent while protection is on, so it travels the same protected path as the rest of your traffic. Turn it off if you would rather your network saw nothing from Shroudly at all.
Start protection to see live traffic.
Split in the middle of SNI
Shroudly is free and runs on donations. If it helps you, you can support it.

Shroudly is free, with no ads and no tracking, and it will stay that way. Donations pay for its servers, code signing and the work of keeping up with new blocks. We share what comes in and what it is spent on.
An international transfer from your bank; this account takes them from more than 150 countries.
